The problem with these games is that they're being sold as video games, but on release they come off as simulations. No Man's Sky was an impressive technological feat, but it wasn't much of a video game. At the end of the day the game is supposed to be fun and if you forget that crucial factor than be prepared for criticism. These games are more like showcases of impressive code. Creating an infinite universe is amazing, but at the end of the day.. what can you do in this universe? It's like if the Grand Theft Auto series didn't have a single player campaign (story missions) to go along with it's vibrant living cities. Without the missions that introduce various new mechanics to keep the players interested the game would get repetitive very quickly.

Then we reach the point of customization. While the universe in these games is beautiful and vibrant, the controls are tight and precise, and all that good stuff, the games seem to forget their roots. What makes an RPG so compelling? In my opinion it's the leveling up process, finding new loot, unlocking new skills, and just everything to do with character customization. I know when I played Destiny, albeit the weapons/armor system were pretty good, the actual player's character lacked much customization. You had your choice between 3 types of grenades, 3 sort of passives to go along with your melee attack, 3 different jump mechanics, and 2 super abilities to choose from. So you can only ever use ONE of these options per category, and you could freely switch back and forth at any time with some rather negligible penalties for doing so. After about a day of messing around with these combinations you've officially played it all. Your character ends up feeling exactly the same as everyone else's, and the lack of variety shows. Look at older games like Diablo 2 and World of Warcraft. The amount of skills you had at your fingertips was outstanding, and the extra layers of customization were compelling. You could truly make your character feel unique. That's what these newer games lack. They simply fall flat when it comes to customization. I felt the same way about Borderlands, you have this decently sized Skill Tree but at the end of the day each character only had about one ability to use. Sure, you can give that single ability an extra effect like "increased size", but it's really not that interesting to use the same thing over and over again, even if it's slightly tweaked.

Anyway, I feel like the lack of customization comes with the territory. You can see that with massive customization comes a price, and that price is usually the amount of effort that goes into the graphics. As of now, you can't have a game like Path of Exile that looks like Anthem. It's clearly just too big of a project to tackle and maybe the technology just isn't there. Hopefully one day we will get a AAA title that looks as beautiful as these newer games that will also have the depth that a lot of hardcore RPG fans desire.
